positions.name: Micron Technology, Inc.
positions.catalyst: NVIDIA cleared the single largest overhang in the market last night and Micron is the most under-reacting way to own the result. NVDA FQ2-27: revenue $96.2B (+106% y/y, +18% q/q) vs ~$92.2B consensus; Data Center $89.0B (+117% y/y); non-GAAP EPS $2.22 vs $2.09 est. The number that matters is the FQ3 guide of $108B — roughly a 12% sequential step-up, several billion above consensus, and guided with ZERO China compute assumed, meaning the figure is pure non-China demand rather than a hopeful re-opening. Every one of those units carries Micron content, and the content per unit is stepping up hard: HBM4 for the Vera Rubin platform began shipping in March and is ramping at ~2x the pace of HBM3E 12-high with yields ahead of plan, and the R100's maximum HBM load goes from 192GB to 288GB on a part reported to be ~80% more expensive per GB-class unit. Micron's entire 2026 HBM output is already sold out under fixed-price contracts, FQ3 guidance is ~$33.5B revenue at 81% gross margin and >$19 EPS, and management has said data centers want ~50% more memory than Micron can ship. Pre-market $975.56 vs $938.40 close = +4.0%, comfortably inside the chase threshold.
positions.driver: The asymmetry is that MU is the cheapest, most liquid, most contractually de-risked name in the group that just got re-rated — and it moved the least. Against the NVDA print, NVDA itself is +6.9%, NBIS +6.3%, CRDO +5.5%, COHR +3.9%; Micron, whose revenue per NVIDIA rack is going UP on the Rubin transition, is only +4.0%. Valuation is the downside protection: 21.1x trailing earnings against a guided >$19 quarterly EPS and 81% gross margin, versus 90x for CRDO and 143x for ALAB, the two obvious higher-beta alternatives. Revenue is contracted, not forecast — 2026 HBM is sold out at fixed prices, so the thesis does not depend on a spot-price cycle holding up over the next 24 hours. There is real overhead room: $975.56 sits ~22% below the June 25 52-week high of $1,255, so this is gap-fill territory rather than blue-sky extension. Liquidity is best-in-class for a 100% book at a $1.06T market cap and 27.7M shares/day average (yesterday traded a light 18.7M into the print, so there is unfilled demand). Critically for a held-through-the-night position, Micron does NOT report until late September — there is no binary event inside the holding window, which is exactly the failure mode that made yesterday's SMTC position uncomfortable. Deliberately passed on the alternatives: MRVL (+4.6%), ADSK, WDAY, AFRM, ULTA, ESTC and RBRK all report TONIGHT after the close and this book does not flatten intraday; OKTA (+19.9%) and CRM (+11.4%) are past the chase threshold; CRWD (+8.9%) is at the threshold, is a software beat that tends to gap-and-fade, and sits within 10% of its Aug 14 52-week high; ALAB and CRDO offer more beta but at 143x and 90x earnings with CRDO's own print due within about a week.
positions.risks: This is a 100% position in a high-beta memory cyclical whose 52-week range is $114.25 to $1,255.00 — an 11x band in twelve months. That range is the risk statement: MU does not trade like a $1T mega-cap, it trades like a levered call on AI capex, and a sentiment crack takes 10%+ out of it quickly. Second, the trade is a sympathy move, not a company-specific event: Micron has released no news of its own, so if the NVDA gap fades intraday — and NVDA's average one-day post-earnings reaction over the prior five quarters was actually NEGATIVE 2.65% despite beating every time — the derivative names fade harder than the principal. That gap-and-fade pattern is the single most likely way this loses. Third, macro: Jackson Hole runs Aug 27-29 with Powell expected Friday morning; the position exits at tomorrow's 6:35am CT run, ahead of the speech, but overnight rate repricing on Thursday's data can still hit a high-multiple semi, and the stop does not protect against an overnight gap. Fourth, memory is a cycle business — the sold-out fixed-price 2026 book that protects near-term revenue also caps upside if spot DRAM/HBM pricing runs, and any hint of 2027 supply additions from Samsung or SK Hynix compresses the multiple immediately. Fifth, NVDA guided $108B assuming zero China; if China policy loosens, that is upside, but the corollary is that the guide already embeds no China cushion if non-China demand disappoints. The stop at $907.27 (-7%) sits below yesterday's entire range (low $924.60, open $925.74), so it is a genuine thesis-invalidation level — a full round-trip of the NVDA gap plus more — rather than noise, but it also means a sharp fade closes the position at a full 7% loss on the whole book.
